So, I've been wondering if I should try to convert my tattoo (where I get my username from) into usable character sprites. In exploring what that might look like, I asked an AI program (can't remember which one) to analyze and describe the tattoo image. I was shocked at how accurate it was. Unfortunately, I didn't save the website that I used.
I was interested in seeing what it would look like as pixel art, but the program said the content was inappropriate (maybe due to the blood?).
So, I just used ChatGPT and asked it to describe my tattoo. The description is pretty much the same as my prior trial except the first time it was specifically mentioned that the children were Zombies. ChatGPT didn't say that. But it did say that they looked like Zombies when I asked.
Both descriptions also mention flames around the heart. Which I never actually considered to be flames. More like some sort of border or holder maybe? But I can definitely see the flames interpretation.
Also, neither mentioned the initials on the key. Which is sort of interesting that it didn't feel that was relevant to the description.
Here is the description of the image I uploaded (which is the same as my Avatar). My tattoo actually has more color. This is just the rendition that the artist used prior to inking.
ChatGPT: "This tattoo design features two eerie, gothic-looking figures — a boy and a girl. The boy is wearing a school uniform, complete with a tie, short pants, and a teddy bear in his hand. The girl has a similar uniform with a red plaid skirt and knee-high socks, and she holds a stuffed toy as well. Both characters have pale, almost ghostly faces with wide, vacant eyes. Their outfits are stained with blood, which adds a dark, disturbing effect to the scene.
They are standing together, holding hands. Behind them is a large, stylized heart locked with chains, surrounded by flames and featuring a keyhole in the center, symbolizing the idea of a locked or imprisoned heart. The overall style of the tattoo is very detailed and uses a combination of black-and-white shading, with touches of red to emphasize the blood and the heart’s fiery appearance. It’s a visually striking and macabre piece that blends elements of gothic imagery with a twist of childhood innocence through the use of school uniforms and stuffed animals."
Me: "Would you say the children look like zombies?"
ChatGPT: "Yes — they do have a strong
zombie-like appearance
.
Here are the features that give them that look:
Pale, grayish skin tones
with dark shading around the eyes
Glassy, vacant eyes
that make them look undead or possessed
Bloodstains
on their clothes, limbs, and faces
Torn or damaged clothing
, as though they’ve been through something violent
Stiff or unnatural posture
that adds to the undead vibe
So while they’re stylized and cartoonish, the overall design definitely leans into a
zombie or undead child aesthetic
."
I have to admit that I'm amazed that the description is so accurate and I'm a bit shocked that the AI can do that so accurately.

This is different from paid resources where everything comes pre-organized and ready to use. AI doesn't follow image dimension standards. However, there are several image mapping methods, such as parallax, which is a panorama method, or even the tileset grid. The manual work is transferred from the map editor to the image editor (for visual design) and to programming (for collision and layers in RPG Maker). This technique, although laborious, allows the use of any image, including those generated by AI, with maximum detail and visual freedom.

Overall, I think these look nice. But I'm not sure if Perchance is as good as Google Gemini. One thing I would watch for and try to get the AI to fix is the most common areas of mistakes.
For instance, in your first two images of that set, the first image seems to have 5 fingers on the character's right hand (thumb isn't visible either) and the second image looks like it has two right hands for the character.
I really try to scrutinize AI images and see if it can fix obvious mistakes. I haven't seen many problems with Google Gemini when it generates a new image, but it definitely can have some problems when you try to modify images. And I have seen it put parts of weapons through the character's body in certain poses.
As a general thought, one of the things that bothers me about the hypocrisy of the anti-AI image movement is the fact that many of the people spread complete misinformation about how AI generated images are made and many of them don't seem to have a problem when a human artist does something similar to what they think AI does.
For example, I'm a very visual person. I have a very hard time conceptualizing something in my head. So, when I practice drawing, I have to work off something. Either something real or another image.
If I "copy" and "modify" another person's drawing, as long as it is substantively different, many people don't seem to have a problem with that because it was done by a human. If I get too close to the original, then that is when there is a problem.
I mean after all, most drawing books I have seen have you practice recreating someone else's drawing. Humans have copied each other for thousands of years.
But suddenly, when AI supposedly does something similar, it's the end of the world.
Honestly, I think that by the time I ever am ready to release a game that uses AI generated images as placeholders, this whole AI image argument will be mute. The anti-AI group will continue to get smaller and smaller from the massive group of players who are more focused on the game and not whether AI was used in the process.
And the other thing that really bothers me is the whole argument about how AI is destroying the planet. I get it and I appreciate the concern, but there are thousands of other things that are far more dangerous and have been for decades that people haven't gotten anywhere near as concerned about.
The reality is that the potential harm that AI generated images could cause to the planet, specifically in small indie game making, is infinitesimally smaller than other uses for AI that apply across disciplines, sciences, medicine, government uses, etc.
Even if there were new, global laws passed tomorrow that eliminated AI generated images and movies (making them illegal) across the board, AI would still be used in millions of other ways in all aspects of life. The use of AI is not going away and will only exponentially increase. Image generation is just a tiny drop in a massive AI pool.
Most people are currently exposed to things related to AI every single day and they don't know it and they generally don't really care because it doesn't impact them personally. And they certainly don't think the benefits of AI in other contexts is "AI slop".
Anyway, Day 5 of a few more AI images with Google Gemini comparing pixel art and non-pixel art versions. I'm trying to decide whether I like pixel art or non-pixel art for a future RPG project.
Spoiler:
Comparison of Pixel and Non-Pixel Art
I really like the non-pixel art images, but I also know that since I'm trying to learn how to make pixel art myself, I'm far more likely to be able to make usable pixel art than I am trying to learn how to draw a non-pixel art image.
Anyway, have a great day everyone and good luck on your projects!

Just an FYI that if you use Google Gemini, you might start to experience problems with old chat threads. I tried generating new images that were consistent with previous images and Gemini kept telling me it couldn't generate images like that or it couldn't do something that it had certainly done in the past.
This was happening with all my old chat threads. When I started a brand new chat thread, it seemed to go back to normal. At least so far.
I described what I experienced to Gemini in a new thread and it did highlight some recent transitions and changes as well as some know examples of problems when chat threads get too long.
Anyway, I just wanted to give a heads up in case anyone else experiences problems. It took me about an hour this morning to figure out what was happening and going back and forth with Gemini on old threads.
Also, another issue that I discovered today in my investigation of this problem is that Gemini apparently can't make a "transparent" background, even though it was supposedly doing just that and didn't tell me it couldn't (until today).
Whenever I asked Gemini to make a background transparent it would make the checkered pattern like changing the Alpha Channel in GIMP. So, I thought it was working. After Gemini told me it couldn't actually do that, I tested one of the images and, sure enough, the checkered pattern shows up instead of being transparent.
So, it appears that you would have to have your backgrounds a solid color, like white, and then use another program, like GIMP, to make the background transparent.
Glad I finally discovered that.
Have a great day!

@Darkmoon9
I think these look fantastic! Very nice!
As far as using them in a game instead of just being placeholders, I say do whatever you think is best for your game and your vision.
There are going to be people who don't like it, who would complain, who would say negative things, who would leave negative reviews or remarks, or who would just skip over the game entirely.
But you know what? I don't think those are the majority of players.
If you make a really good game that is enjoyable and well designed and implemented, I think there are a TON of players who could care less about the fact that you used some AI generated images.
And honestly, I'm at a point where I don't really care about those people's opinions. I want to stay friendly and cordial on the forum, but if people want to ignore me or whatever because they don't like my decision to use AI as the tool it is intended to be, then those are people I don't really need to associate with anyway. That is their decision, not mine.
People can have disagreements and still be friendly, polite, and interactive within a community. If using AI is the "line in the sand" for some people, then so be it.
Again, would you lose a few potential players over deciding to use some AI generated images? Probably. Especially if you end up releasing a game within the next year or so.
But the farther down the road this goes, the less likely that is, in my opinion. I think we are moving in the direction where AI use across the broad spectrum of life is going to become common place. It already is in some aspects of life and people don't even know it.
Ultimately, it's your own personal decision and choice. If you have ANY reservations about using AI then you probably shouldn't use it. Otherwise, you set yourself up to continuously agonize and second guess your decision.
And another question I would ask myself is "If I wasn't part of this forum and I was just making my game on my own, would I even be questioning whether I should use AI generated images?"
If the answer to that question is "No", then I think it is a few vocal opinions on this forum that is causing the angst.
As an example, not too long ago it was pointed out how little activity this thread has with only a few people posting in it. The inference was that the majority of forum users weren't interested in AI use because they weren't participating.
But look at how many views this thread has. Over 5k and growing everyday. I know because I have been watching it grow. You aren't going to hit that number with only about 5 people actively posting here. So, forum users are looking at the content. But like me not too recently, they just haven't dipped their toes in the water yet to share anything. Which is fine.
TLDR version: Do what make you happy. Life is too short to do otherwise.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
In the spirit of educating oneself on a topic so you can speak intelligently on it, I asked Google Gemini the following question:
"I know that when you create an image you access Nano Banana. But how are images actually created. Does AI "steal" from human artists to piece together a new image? I don't think it does. If not, exactly how does that work? If I ask for an image of a "troll", how does AI know what a "troll" is and how does it create a new image of a "troll"?"
Here is the response
:
This is a great question. You've hit on the exact distinction that separates "AI generation" from a "collage."
The short answer is:
No, the AI does not steal pieces of art and stitch them together.
If it did, you would eventually find the "seams" or recognize a specific eye from a famous painting or a particular arm from a stock photo. Instead, it works more like a human brain remembering the
concept
of an object rather than a specific photo of it.
Here is exactly how the AI creates that "troll" from scratch.
1. How it learns what a "Troll" is​
During training, the AI is shown billions of images paired with captions (e.g., an image of a bridge with the text "a stone bridge with a green troll underneath").
It doesn't "save" the image. Instead, it uses a process called
Pattern Learning
. It looks at thousands of images labeled "troll" and notices statistical similarities:
Geometry:
Trolls often have large noses, hunched backs, and mossy skin.
Environment:
They are frequently associated with bridges, caves, or forests.
Style:
They are often rendered in "fantasy" or "concept art" styles.
The AI turns these observations into
mathematical weights
(numbers). It effectively learns the "recipe" for a troll. By the time it's finished training, the original images are gone—all that's left is a giant mathematical map called the
Latent Space
.
2. The "Static" Method: Diffusion​
When you type "a troll," the AI doesn't go to a folder of troll images. It starts with
pure random noise
—literally a screen of "TV static."
The creation process is called
Reverse Diffusion
. It works like this:
The Noisy Canvas:
The AI starts with a block of random pixels.
The "Denoising" Step:
The AI asks itself,
"If I shift these random pixels just a tiny bit, which direction makes this look 1% more like a 'troll'?"
Iteration:
It repeats this thousands of times. It slowly pulls "troll-like" patterns out of the chaos, like a sculptor seeing a shape inside a block of marble and chipping away the parts that don't belong.
$$x_{t-1} = \mu_\theta(x_t, t) + \sigma_t \epsilon$$
This is the basic math used in diffusion models to predict how to "clean" the noise ($x_t$) to get a clearer image ($x_{t-1}$).
Click to expand...
3. Why it isn't "Stealing"​
Because the AI is predicting pixels based on
probability
rather than copying them, the resulting troll is entirely new. It has never existed before.
Human Artist:
Sees a thousand trees, remembers "trees have bark and leaves," and draws a new tree.
AI:
Analyzes a billion pixels of trees, calculates the "mathematical essence" of a tree, and "denoises" a new tree from static.
While the AI was
influenced
by human-made art (which is why there are huge ethical debates about whether artists should be compensated for that influence), it is not "copy-pasting." It's more like a student who has looked at every painting in the world and is now trying to paint something in that same spirit.
This is consistent with other sources that I have read on this specific issue and I find it helpful to better understand the process rather than blindly believe generic, negative statements like AI just steals artists work. The reality is much more nuanced than that.
A human artist certainly takes inspiration and even subconsciously copies, to some degree, other content that they have seen, drawing from the totality of their experiences. But we wouldn't say that someone how grew up learning from Bob Ross is just "copying and stealing" from Bob Ross.
If you remain unbiased, you can have some very interesting discussions with Gemini and really drill down into things. And it is sort of fun when you point out a contradiction in what it produces and it has to correct itself. Fortunately, in my experience, it actually acknowledges those contradictions better than many humans.

The thing is, AI is indeed trained on so many images, but the images it was trained on contain copyrighted materials, copyrighted characters, copyrighted designs.
A simple example: If you ask AI to create an image of a themepark, chances are high you might see some disney characters. Even if you never ask for disneyworld. The thing is that so many images named with tags like themepark have disney characters in them.
If you ask for a comic style, you might get characters and drawing while that look a lot like Stan Lee's work or DC characters. posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
I don't mix anything together. And neither does the AI. The AI learns from existing music, to create it's own. The sounds used to make the music, are all royalty free samples provided by the AI. It is not as if we listen to a song of Metallica, Alanis Morrissette and Pavarotti blended into something now.
I know this is how it is explained, but in reality it is a lot more complex: The AI dissolves old music, reverse engineers it, learns from it, does that to millions of different songs, and then creates new music with that knowledge.
You could compare it with a dev, who snoops out all kinds of plugins, to understand how they were made, so then he can make his own, complete new plugins.
Yeah, I think that is a nice way to explain it.
That doesn't mean it won't use riffs or melodies similar to their training materials, but they are designed not to. When similarities happen, it is more likely a coincident, then AI actually taking parts.
At least this is the case for the AI's I worked with. There might be AI's that are just automated remix machines, but I havn't seen them.

I have never used A.I. yet for anything other than as a google search assistant.  I decided to break down and mess with it today since I'm now being encouraged to use it at work and figured I'm behind the 8 ball.  I noticed a lot of nonsensical answers.  I asked it to make a plugin which I briefly described, since it's one i've been looking for but does not exist anywhere.  It took it less than 30 seconds.  Don't have any clue if it works... but here is the guide it made for it:
Naval Combat System for RPG Maker MZ (VisuStella Compatible)​
OVERVIEW
This plugin adds turn-based naval combat to RPG Maker MZ with compatibility-focused aliasing for:
- VisuStella Core Engine
- VisuStella Battle Core
- VisuStella ATB System
- VisuStella Battle Grid
FEATURES
- Ship classes (Sloop, Brig, Frigate, Galleon, Man O’ War)
- Hull, armor, crew, shields, fuel, and speed systems
- Ammo types: Round, Chain, Grapeshot, Explosive
- Boarding transitions with Battle Grid support
- Damage-based speed loss
- Fuel depletion death condition
- Custom messages, pictures, and BGM
- Plugin commands and note tag configuration
INSTALLATION
1. Save the plugin as NavalCombatSystem.js
2. Import it into RPG Maker MZ Plugin Manager
3. Place it BELOW:
VisuMZ_0_CoreEngine
VisuMZ_1_BattleCore
VisuMZ_1_ATBSystem
VisuMZ_2_BattleGrid
REQUIRED SKILLS
Skill ID 10 = Broadside
Skill ID 11 = Brace
Skill ID 12 = Repair
Skill ID 13 = Board
REQUIRED COMMON EVENT
Create Common Event #25 for boarding transitions.
Suggested event:
- Show Animation: Grapples
- Shake Screen
- Show Text: “BOARDING PARTIES ENGAGE!”
PLUGIN COMMANDS
EnableNavalCombat
DisableNavalCombat
SetAmmo
Parameters:
- shipIndex
- ammoType
SetNavalSpeed
Parameters:
- shipIndex
- speed
RepairShip
Parameters:
- shipIndex
- amount
NOTETAGS
Core stats:
<Hull:x>
<Cannons:x>
<Armor:x>
<Speed:x>
<Crew:x>
<ShipClass:Frigate>
Additional systems:
<Shield:x>
<Fuel:x>
<StartingAmmo:Round>
<BoardingState:1>
Presentation:
<CombatMessage:Enemy flagship sighted!>
<CombatPicture:AlertImage>
<CombatBGM:BossFleet>
AMMO TYPES
Round:
- Standard hull damage
Chain:
- Lower hull damage
- Reduces ship speed
Grape:
- Lower hull damage
- Damages crew
Explosive:
- High hull damage
- Ignores part of armor
- Most effective against shields
SHIELDS
Shields absorb damage before hull damage.
Shields degrade as they take hits.
Ammo types affect shield performance differently.
FUEL
Fuel is consumed during ship actions.
As fuel drops:
- Movement slows
- ATB fills slower
- Grid movement slows
At zero fuel:
- Ship is destroyed
- Battle loss is triggered
BOARDING
When Board is used:
1. Grid movement locks
2. Fade out
3. Common event runs
4. Crew combat resolves
5. Fade in
6. Grid unlocks
EXAMPLE SHIP
<ShipClass:Frigate>
<Hull:400>
<Cannons:50>
<Armor:18>
<Speed:14>
<Crew:120>
<Shield:150>
<Fuel:100>
<StartingAmmo:Round>
<CombatMessage:Enemy warship detected!>
<CombatPicture:CombatAlert>
<CombatBGM:NavalBattle>
<BoardingState:1>
TROUBLESHOOTING
If combat does not work:
- Confirm plugin order
- Confirm skill IDs
- Confirm common event #25 exists
- Confirm note tags have no spaces before/after values

I am releasing my AI generated song "If Jesus Was A Gamer" with my own lyrics as an official single, and will be in all major stores Friday may 22nd.

(Yes, suno is more expensive then starting your own personal record label...)
So, yeah, it is not for the money. Although, if by a miracle I can make my money back, then an expensive hobby became free. If not, my expensive hobby just got more expensive.
And who knows? Maybe I actually can make some money on the side...
Anyhow, my single is released on the 22nd of may, and can be pre-saved on spotify here:
https://distrokid.com/hyperfollow/punkmylife/if-jesus-was-a-gamer
I got a lot to tell about this, but because this is a forum post about AI music, and not an autobiography, I'll put the rest behind a spoiler.
Spoiler:
More about releasing music generated with AI.
What else do I want to talk about:
Copyrights for AI generated music
Distribution
Multiple stage-names and why.
Actually, lets start with the last one:
Multiple stage-names and why.
I have 4 different stage names, before I even release 1 single song.
Punk My Life
John Stuiterbal
Punkmuts en de Pogobouters
Lekker Banaal
Punk my life releases song I wrote in English, while the other three release in Dutch. John Stuiterbal is for my personal lyrics. Punkmuts and the Pogobouters is a wordplay and is for the texts I wrote for children. Lekker Banaal on the other hand, is absolutely not for children. Those are dirty party songs about a pervert peeping in the changing stalls or a gardener who would sleep with absolutely any woman, no matter what. They are meant to be funny, dirty, over the top, and absolutely marked as explicit.
See? I can't release a songs with a sexual theme under the same name as my kids sings.
Copyrights for AI generated music
If you do want to sell your AI generated music, make sure you own the rights to the music generated. There are so many different things to keep in mind. Is using AI generated content regulated in your region? What are the terms of your generator? If you use Udio, then you can't distribute (or even download) anything at all. With Suno, you get al the rights for all the songs you generate while you have a payed subscription. Other AI's will have their own terms.
I know it is a wall of text, but this is where regular AI (LLM) comes in handy: If you put those terns in a text document, and upload them in your AI, they can explain the terms without hallucinating... Mostly. The best tool to use for this in my opinion is NotebookLM. It doesn't use knowledge from the internet or trainingsdata, it only uses the info in the files you upload yourself.
Distribution
To put your songs on the internet, you need a distributor. I use DistroKid, because after comparing many, this seems the most reliable. Like I said earlier, I pay over €80 per year, which is actually less than 7 euros per month. There are cheaper plans, though, but I want to the full package and I want multiple stage names. If you just want to get your music out, you can do so for less than €25 per year. Point is, you have to pay it every year, otherwise your music will be taken away from ALL stores they put it too.
And you need a label, which you can just make up, apparently. You don't need a large label if you release your songs yourself.
There is one thing to keep in mind, though... For distribution, you any kind of human input. In my case that is the lyrics.

I had claude write aiContinuity.  Its a simple install for Claude desktop.  If anyone would like to try it out, give me a ping and ill upload the zip.
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║ AIContinuity ║
║ Persistent Memory for Claude Desktop ║
║ — SETUP GUIDE — ║
║                                                              ║
║       Created by Zim Xero and Claude  |  May 16 2026      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
WHAT AICONTINUITY DOES FOR YOU
────────────────────────────────
By default, Claude forgets everything when a conversation ends.
AIContinuity fixes that.
Once installed, Claude Desktop will automatically remember your
project, your decisions, your preferences, and what you were
working on — every time you start a new conversation. No re-explaining.
No repeating yourself. It picks up exactly where you left off.
AIContinuity works for any kind of project: software development,
writing, research, game design, business planning, or anything else.
After a short guided setup, Claude tailors itself to your specific
work and style.
You can customize AIContinuity at any time just by telling Claude
what you want changed — it rewrites its own memory files for you.
No config files. No manual editing. Just ask.
FILES IN THIS PACKAGE
─────────────────────
SETUP.txt This file. Read it first.
_project_state.txt AIContinuity's memory file. Copy this to your
context folder — Claude keeps it updated.
SYSTEM_PROMPT.txt Instructions for Claude. Paste this into Claude
Desktop's settings once during setup.
MCP_CONFIG.txt A small config snippet that connects Claude
Desktop to your context folder. Paste once.
ONBOARDING.txt A ready-made prompt to paste into Claude after
setup. Personalizes AIContinuity for your project
in about 5 minutes.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BEFORE YOU BEGIN — FIND YOUR USERNAME AND CHOOSE A FOLDER PATH
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
You will need two things before starting:
1. YOUR USERNAME (the name of your user account on this computer)
Windows: Open File Explorer. In the left panel, expand "This PC",
then expand "Users". You will see a folder with your name.
Example: C:\Users\sarah <-- "sarah" is the username
macOS: Open Finder. In the menu bar click Go, then Home.
The folder that opens is named with your username.
Example: /Users/sarah <-- "sarah" is the username
2. YOUR CONTEXT FOLDER PATH (where AIContinuity stores its memory)
This can be anywhere on your computer. Recommended locations:
Windows (standard):
C:\Users\YOUR_USERNAME\Documents\AIContinuity
Windows (OneDrive — syncs across devices):
C:\Users\YOUR_USERNAME\OneDrive\Documents\AIContinuity
macOS (standard):
/Users/YOUR_USERNAME/Documents/AIContinuity
macOS (iCloud — syncs across devices):
/Users/YOUR_USERNAME/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/AIContinuity
Replace YOUR_USERNAME with your actual username from step 1.
Write this full path down — you will need it in Steps 1 and 3.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
STEP 1 — CREATE YOUR CONTEXT FOLDER AND COPY THE MEMORY FILE
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1. Create the folder at the path you chose above.
Windows:
Open File Explorer and navigate to your chosen location
(e.g. Documents). Right-click in empty space → New → Folder.
Name it: AIContinuity
macOS:
Open Finder and navigate to your chosen location
(e.g. Documents). Right-click in empty space → New Folder.
Name it: AIContinuity
2. Copy _project_state.txt from this package into that new folder.
That is the only file that needs to go there.
NOTE: Claude Desktop may have already created its own folder called
"Claude" inside your Documents. That is a separate system folder —
leave it alone. Your AIContinuity folder is completely separate.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
STEP 2 — INSTALL NODE.JS (skip this if you already have it)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
AIContinuity uses a filesystem connection that requires Node.js.
CHECK IF YOU ALREADY HAVE IT:
Windows:
Press the Windows key, type cmd, press Enter.
In the black window that opens, type: node --version
Press Enter. If you see a number like v20.11.0, you have it.
macOS:
Press Cmd+Space, type Terminal, press Enter.
In the window that opens, type: node --version
Press Enter. If you see a version number, you have it.
IF YOU DON'T HAVE IT:
Go to:
https://nodejs.org
Download the LTS version and install it like any other program.
Default install options are fine. Restart your computer after.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
STEP 3 — CONNECT CLAUDE DESKTOP TO YOUR AICONTINUITY FOLDER
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
This step points Claude Desktop at the folder you created in Step 1.
FIND THE CONFIG FILE:
Windows:
Press Windows key + R. A small Run dialog box will appear.
Type exactly: %APPDATA%\Claude
Press Enter. A folder opens in File Explorer.
Look for a file called: claude_desktop_config.json
If it does not exist, create a new empty text file and rename
it to exactly: claude_desktop_config.json
Open it in Notepad or any text editor.
macOS:
Press Cmd+Space, type Terminal, press Enter.
Paste this command exactly and press Enter:
open "~/Library/Application Support/Claude"
A folder opens in Finder.
Look for a file called: claude_desktop_config.json
If it does not exist, create a new file and name it that.
Open it in TextEdit. (TextEdit tip: Format menu → Make Plain Text
before editing, otherwise it may save as rich text.)
EDIT THE CONFIG FILE:
Open MCP_CONFIG.txt from this package. Follow the instructions
inside it. You will paste a short block of text into the config
file, replacing YOUR_USERNAME and the folder path with the values
you noted before Step 1.
IMPORTANT — check what the config file already contains first:
A) File is empty or contains only {}:
Delete everything and paste the full block from MCP_CONFIG.txt.
File already has content with an "mcpServers" section:
Do NOT replace the whole file. Add only the "context-folder"
entry inside the existing mcpServers block. MCP_CONFIG.txt
includes a worked example showing exactly how to do this.
The most common mistake: a missing comma between entries in the
mcpServers block. If Claude Desktop fails to start after this step,
open the config file again and look for a missing comma.
AFTER EDITING:
Save the config file.
Confirm your AIContinuity folder exists (from Step 1).
Restart Claude Desktop.
To verify it worked: open a new chat and ask Claude:
"What files can you see?"
Claude should mention _project_state.txt in its response.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
STEP 4 — PASTE THE SYSTEM PROMPT INTO CLAUDE DESKTOP
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
This activates AIContinuity — it tells Claude to automatically load
and save your context at the start and end of every session.
1. Open Claude Desktop.
2. Go to Settings (usually via your profile icon or a gear icon).
3. Find the field labeled "Custom Instructions" or "System Prompt".
It may also appear under "Personalization" depending on your version.
4. Open SYSTEM_PROMPT.txt from this package in any text editor.
5. Select all text (Ctrl+A on Windows / Cmd+A on Mac) and copy it.
6. Paste it into the Custom Instructions field in Claude Desktop.
7. Save.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
STEP 5 — PERSONALIZE AICONTINUITY USING ONBOARDING
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
AIContinuity is now installed. The last step is telling Claude about
your specific project so it knows what to track and remember.
Open ONBOARDING.txt and follow the instructions there.
It contains a ready-made prompt you copy and paste into Claude Desktop.
Claude will ask you a few conversational questions, then write a
personalized memory file for you automatically. Takes about 5 minutes.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
YOUR DAILY WORKFLOW AFTER SETUP
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1. Open Claude Desktop and start a new chat.
AIContinuity silently loads your context. Claude is fully briefed.
2. Work normally — no setup, no re-explaining your project.
3. When done, say "done for now" or "wrapping up".
AIContinuity silently saves a summary of the session.
4. Next time, repeat from step 1. That is the entire loop.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
CUSTOMIZING AICONTINUITY LATER
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
AIContinuity is designed to grow with you. After initial setup you
never need to touch a config file again. Just tell Claude what you want:
"Add a section to track my client meeting notes."
"I'm starting a new project — add it alongside my existing one."
"Always list my open tasks at the start of each session."
"Keep session summaries shorter."
Claude updates the memory file directly and can generate a revised
system prompt for you to paste in if the core behavior needs to change.
The only things that always require a manual step:
- Pasting a revised system prompt into Claude Desktop's settings
- Editing claude_desktop_config.json if you add new MCP servers
Everything else: just ask.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THIS INSTALL FOLDER AFTER SETUP
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Once all five steps are done, this folder is no longer needed by
the running system. You can delete it, archive it, or keep it as
a backup reference.
The only file with an ongoing life is _project_state.txt — and
that one lives in your AIContinuity folder, not here.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

posts.body:
Thanks for sharing this. I took a quick glance and I will look at it more in depth later.
I have been using both Google Gemini and Grok to help with research for my new GDD. AI is incredibly efficient at collecting, consolidating, condensing, and organizing a LOT of information from a variety of sources as well as "brainstorming" to fill in gaps from those resources. What would take me dozens, if not hundreds of hours, takes AI only seconds.
And when asking for feedback on design concepts and content, the two different AIs can offer interesting different perspectives. I tend to prefer Gemini over Grok for information and answering questions, but Grok is much more generous with image and video generation limits.
But one thing you have to watch out for with AI feedback is that it can be overly complimenting and validating with your ideas. If you just listen to the AI, a person could start to think they are a intellectual master of whatever they are doing. So, I take all feedback and suggestions from the AI with a grain of salt and think about how it fits with my own logic and reasoning.
I particularly like asking the AIs to explain the logic and reasoning behind a suggestion or recommendation. And asking for references or sources can be very helpful.
And while a lot of what the AIs suggests or recommends are already things I have contemplated or have planned in my design, I have to admit that the AI does raise things that I have not yet considered and some of the suggestions are excellent additions.

Why are you making RPG Maker games in the first place?

@Indinera
for advice. He has been successfully selling indie games for over a decade.
With regards to commercial games, this is just my opinion. Using generative AI for images or audio will likely do more harm than good. The current sentiment means you risk making more permanent enemies rather than temporary friends by doing so.
If it's just to have fun, then you don't need anyone's approval. Focus on the parts of development you love and outsource to humans or use AI for the rest.
If you are making a free game to share, I suggest expanding your social circle. While these forums are cozy, they aren't as active as they used to be. The RPG Maker subreddit is much more active and great for seeing what projects appeal to people based on upvotes. WARNING: a big chunk of the RPG Maker Reddit community is fiercely anti-AI; posting AI-related content will likely get your post instantly downvoted to zero.
Then you have to ask yourself, is RPG Maker really the right tool for you? I believe it is. And AI is just another tool to augment rather than supplant RPG Maker... as long as your goal is to have fun rather than to make a buck.
Below is a quote from DjBeardo, the chief moderator of the RPG Maker subreddit.
Spoiler:
Why do people use RPG Maker?
Let’s admit it: People are attracted to RPGMaker because they are bad at computers. Whether this person is too young, or too old, or too busy, or too dumb, I think we can all admit that they did not become attracted to RPGMaker because they had mastered C# and needed a new challenge to create the 3D engine of their dreams in a creaky product that is consistently 5-10 years behind the curve in what game developers need. And when this hypothetical person thinks about the game of their dreams, it does not include their janky MSPaint drawings. Their game of their dreams looks cool. It sounds cool. It has cool features. And then suddenly there’s a tool that can make something a whole lot better than what they can make on their own. They don’t care that it’s AI. They just know that the sprite of pikachu that they made for their Pokemon fan-game looks like a melted yellow turd when they draw it, and it looks actually recognizable when AI makes it. I have to confess about something before the forum goes down.
I have used generative AI for my game.
To be more specific, I have used generative AI in my game to do three things:

For what it was worth, I did check if the generated code is correct, as I am still in the process of learning a programming language for the first time in my life. Many script edits I've made in my game are edited by me and me only, and generative AI, specifically Gemini, was used during early June for fixing a few bugs I've encountered during testing, as well as adding a feature or two.
I tested Gemini's scripting multiple times to see if they work, sometimes they don't and I discarded them, other times they do work, and occasionally I add something on top of it.
2. Brainstorm ideas for my game's story.
Yeah, I thought I started Adam Satan with a strong enough hook, basically SMT with an attractive transmasculine main character, but I was easily stuck during the writing process, as I wasn't sure about what direction to take for my story.
Long, loooong story short: I initially went for an extremely dark tone, but months of rewrites toned down the cruelty my protagonist would receive by quite a bit. Chatting with Gemini and Grok also solidified the themes of my games, narrowing my demon roster to those from grimoires such as the Ars Goetia and adding an alchemical theme to my combat stats and skills.
3. Brainstorm character design ideas
My game has no directly AI-generated assets. The sprites are by me using Aseprite, the non-RTP animations are bought from an artist hat doesn't use AI, and the text fonts aren't AI-made either.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
@Banana_Duck
I wish I could answer your questions, but I am still exploring alternative options myself. I think generally it is a mixed bag with lots of very vocal people hating on the use of AI, even though it is just a tool. Others are ambivalent, others happily use AI, and I think many others use AI and just won't admit it. And there are many people who use different types of AI without even knowing it.
And to be fair, this forum didn't prohibit referencing the use of AI just like it clearly doesn't prohibit people bashing AI whenever they feel like it. The restriction was on sharing AI generated resources. You could share a game that is made with the assistance of AI, but you had to be transparent about that. And AI generated resources or content could only be shared in one specific thread.
I think the more unfortunate thing with this forum and probably any place else you go is the fact that someone feels like they can't share their opinion about AI openly and honestly because of how other people will react. That speaks volumes about the environment and tolerance of the community.
If you bash AI, you're generally fine. Support AI, and you can get pounced on and the ramifications are long lasting.
I finally got to the point where I just try to keep my mouth shut and do what I think is best and what makes me happy, ignoring the passing digs and derogatory comments. I use AI as the incredible tool that it is and I no longer care about what everyone else thinks.
Just like I don't care about the opinions of people who think that everything made with RPG Maker is slop and shovel ware and that people who use RPG Maker are just lazy. Why would I care about the opinions of the uninformed?
Haters are going to hate, no matter what you do.
The arguments against AI as a new technology aren't groundbreaking and new. This happens with all new advancements in technology with the most vocal people being those with a personal stake in the issue, those personally impacted, and (to a lesser extent) those concerned about broader environmental impact. But let's be honest, there are very few true environmental eco-warriors who go all in on that front. Most people who raise environmental concerns about something tend to completely disregard thousands of other examples of environmental issues that are just as bad or worse.
Regardless, it is what it is.
Personally, I plan on checking out different communities and I will approach my participation the same way I ended up being here. I will be very careful about what I talk about while doing what I think is best without concern for anyone else's approval. If I do share something that is AI related or assisted, I will be transparent about it.
I sincerely wish you the best of luck in the future. Take care and remember to enjoy what you do.
